newsitem.title: GERMANY: German "Wise Man" repeats call for EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: German "Wise Man" repeats call for EMU delay.

text.p: A key economic advisor to the German government said again European monetary union (EMU) should be delayed by one to two years, as it would be impossible for enough countries to meet the entry rules by the January 1999 start date.

Rolf Peffekoven, a member of Germany's Council of Economic Advisers known as the "Five Wise Men", told Wednesday's Express newspaper that high German unemployment was hampering efforts to reduce the deficit to three percent of economic output.
But he said Bonn could not risk softening the convergence criteria.

"Since it will not be possible to make the January 1, 1999 start date with as many countries as possible and strict adherence to the criteria, concessions will have to be made on one of these goals," Peffekoven said in the interview.
"Since a softening of the convergence criteria cannot be considered, and rightly so, EMU must be delayed by one to two years," he said.

The Five Wise Men, who advise the government in an annual report on economic policy, have previously called for a delay, saying Germany is unlikely to meet the EMU targets this year, the key year for deciding the starting line-up for EMU under the existing timetable.
Peffekoven said he believed German unemployment would average 4.2 million this year, meaning that no real improvement could be expected in the labour market.
"It will therefore be difficult (for Germany) to meet the 3.0 percent deficit criterion," he said.

"Since tax increases are out of the question, there must be further cuts in public spending, including social spending, which make up 30 percent of gross domestic product. Social spending must be more strongly focused on the truly needy."
